# Five texture ideas, one sheet -- PLA, nozzle 205C, bed 60C, M221 S100

**Not yet print-tested.** Generated by `ideas_test.mjs five-ideas-sheet`; none of these is a library function. Same textures and parameters as the five single files from the same day, only moved and packed closer together.

Calibration line: `freeformSolid` x=120-180, y=45, printed first. Part fan on (`M106 S255`) after it, off at the end. Before each block the nozzle retracts and lifts to Z5, so travel between blocks clears everything already printed. `verifyLayout` (3mm min gap, all 25 regions): ok=true, 0 warnings.

| block | area on the bed | print order |
|---|---|---|
| Fish scales | x 19-60, y 20-62 | 1 |
| Donut / crater dots | x 22-65, y 70-134 | 2 |
| Sawtooth ridges | x 71-139, y 55-87 | 3 |
| Density-gradient stipple | x 72-122, y 96-164 | 4 |
| Woven over-under | x 145-201, y 55-111 | 5 |

## Fish scales

Each scale: anchor puddle (Z 0.2->0.5, e 0.2) -> strand ramps +X over length L up to the tip height (e/d 0.05, F300) -> 500ms dwell -> retract -> 0.8mm dry pull to snap the tail -> lift. Scales point +X and each row is printed from its +X end, so later scales lie on the bases of earlier ones. "Overlap clearance" is how far the new strand runs above the one beneath (aim >= 0.4mm, one strand thickness).

| id | position (x0, y0) | parameters | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | 19.0, 20.0 | L 4, tip 1mm, pitch 5, 8 scales | single tongues, no overlap -- baseline |
| F2 | 19.0, 28.0 | L 4, tip 1.5mm, pitch 5, 8 scales | steeper, higher tip, no overlap |
| F3 | 19.0, 36.0 | L 4, tip 1.3mm, pitch 2, 12 scales, overlap clearance 0.40mm | overlapping tiles, half-length pitch |
| F4 | 19.0, 44.0 | L 5, tip 1.7mm, pitch 2, 12 scales, overlap clearance 0.48mm | longer overlapping tiles |
| F5 | 19.0, 55.0 | 4 rows, 1.5mm apart, L 4, tip 1.3, pitch 2 | staggered 2D patch (4 rows x 10), the fish-skin field |

**What to look for**: Stroke each row toward +X (with the grain) and toward -X (against it): is there a clear difference? Do the tips stay raised or droop flat? In F3/F4/F5, did the overlapping strands fuse into a sheet or stay separate tiles? Did the dry pull leave clean tips or strings?

## Donut / crater dots

Each ring is the library's spiralDisc() with 0.42mm turns, trimmed to the annulus and printed through emitStroke() (0.42 bead, F250), one layer at a time. D6 is the existing circularDot as a solid reference.

| id | position (x0, y0) | parameters | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 23.0, 70.0 | OD 3, hole 1.2, wall 0.9, 2 layers (0.4mm), 5 @ 9mm | small ring |
| D2 | 22.5, 79.5 | OD 4, hole 1.6, wall 1.2, 3 layers (0.6mm), 5 @ 9mm | medium ring |
| D3 | 22.0, 89.0 | OD 5, hole 2.5, wall 1.3, 3 layers (0.6mm), 5 @ 9mm | larger ring, half-diameter hole |
| D4 | 21.5, 98.5 | OD 6, hole 3.6, wall 1.2, 3 layers (0.6mm), 5 @ 9mm | thin-walled ring |
| D5 | 21.5, 108.5 | OD 6, hole 3.6, wall 1.2, 5 layers (1.0mm), 5 @ 9mm | as D4 but 1.0mm tall -- a crater |
| D6 | 22.5, 119.5 | solid D 4, 3 layers | CONTROL: solid circularDot, same size/height as D2 |
| D7 | 23.0, 130.0 | OD 3, hole 1.2, wall 0.9, 3 layers (0.6mm), 10 @ 4mm | ring line: rings 4mm apart, nearly touching |

**What to look for**: Can you feel the hole in each size (where does it stop reading as a ring and start reading as a dot)? Compare D2 with D6 directly. Did the small holes (D1, D7) close up with ooze?

## Sawtooth ridges

Ridges run along X and repeat along +Y. Each layer is a solid strip of 0.45mm-spaced beads (serpentine, F1200, e/d 0.0374); layer k is (1 - (k-1)/n) of the pitch wide. Asymmetric patches keep the strip pinned to the ridge's -Y edge, so that face is vertical and the slope descends toward +Y. Patches are printed layer by layer across all ridges.

| id | position (x0, y0) | parameters | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 71.0, 55.0 | 6 ridges x 30mm along X, pitch 2, 5 layers (1.0mm) | asymmetric, fine: 2mm pitch, 1.0mm tall |
| S2 | 107.0, 55.0 | 4 ridges x 30mm along X, pitch 3, 8 layers (1.6mm) | asymmetric, coarse: 3mm pitch, 1.6mm tall |
| S3 | 71.0, 73.0 | 4 ridges x 30mm along X, pitch 3, 8 layers (1.6mm) | SYMMETRIC control for S2 (same pitch and height) |
| S4 | 107.0, 73.0 | 3 ridges x 30mm along X, pitch 4, 5 layers (1.0mm) | asymmetric, shallow: 4mm pitch, 1.0mm tall |

**What to look for**: Stroke S1/S2/S4 along +Y (down the slopes) and -Y (into the steep faces): is the direction obvious? Compare S2 with S3, which has the same size but no direction. Did the vertical face stay vertical or slump?

## Density-gradient stipple

Every dot is the library's circularDot (spiral disc, 0.4mm tall). Gradients run along +X across a 50mm field: low X = dense / small, high X = sparse / large.

| id | position (x0, y0) | parameters | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 72.0, 96.0 | 50x14mm, 76 dots, height 0.4 | CONTROL: uniform hex, 3mm |
| P2 | 72.0, 114.0 | 50x14mm, 57 dots, height 0.4 | hex, spacing grades 2 -> 6mm along +X |
| P3 | 72.0, 132.0 | 50x14mm, 37 dots, height 0.4, seed 20261029 | random (seeded), min spacing grades 2 -> 6mm |
| P4 | 72.0, 150.0 | 50x14mm, 56 dots, height 0.4 | hex 3.5mm, dot DIAMETER grades 0.8 -> 2.4mm |

**What to look for**: Sweep a finger along +X: does P2/P3 feel like a smooth rough-to-smooth change, or in steps? Is the random field (P3) more pleasant than the hex (P2)? Does a size gradient (P4) read as strongly as a spacing gradient?

## Woven over-under

Warp = lines along X, weft = lines along Y, bead 0.5 x 0.2, F900. Layer 1: full warp lines; weft lines broken 0.6mm either side of every warp line. Layers 2 and 3 (Z 0.4, 0.6): at each crossing, a 2.4mm bump on whichever thread is 'over' -- on the warp it sits on the warp; on the weft it bridges the break and crosses on top of the warp. The 'under' thread stays broken, so it reads as passing beneath. A real under-pass is not printable (the nozzle can't fit under a strand), so this is a relief imitation.

| id | position (x0, y0) | parameters | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | 145.0, 55.0 | 24x24mm, 6 x 6 lines | plain weave, 4mm grid |
| W2 | 175.0, 55.0 | 24x24mm, 8 x 8 lines | plain weave, 3mm grid |
| W3 | 145.0, 85.0 | 24x24mm, 8 x 8 lines | 2/2 twill, 3mm grid -- diagonal ribs |
| W4 | 175.0, 85.0 | 24x24mm, 6 x 6 lines | CONTROL: plain crosshatch, no over/under |

**What to look for**: Does W1/W2 read as fabric under the finger compared with W4? Does the twill (W3) give a diagonal grain? Did the weft bridges over the breaks hold or sag into gaps?

Totals: 46443 G-code lines, 1317 retractions, 876.1 mm commanded filament.
